originality.rationale: Compared the entire mathematical implication of the heterogeneous diagonal similarity, principal killing exponent and full Doob generator, not merely titles. Shiatis (2026) states the copies of one common Markov chain and illustrates homogeneous ring walkers; Johnston (2025) supplies the homogeneous cyclic sine eigenfunction; Bisi et al. (2023) treats particle-inhomogeneous discrete-time exclusion on the line with an RSK/Fredholm construction, not conditional survival of independent unequal-rate Poisson particles on a finite ring. Six published-record queries and targeted general web searches did not find a theorem with the given simultaneous rate-gauge identity and conditioned-generator invariance. All classical inputs are credited. Search non-detection does not prove priority; although the complete accessible Johnston arXiv preprint and Johnston–Shiatis arXiv preprint were consulted at their relevant proofs, unindexed general gauge arguments remain documented residual risks.
residual_risks: An unindexed general diagonal-gauge or exponential-tilting result for labeled finite-ring walkers might imply the claimed similarity.

The publisher journal edition of Johnston was paywalled; its open-access arXiv v6 preprint and the Johnston–Shiatis v4 arXiv preprint were instead consulted. Unindexed or non-arXiv revisions may remain uninspected.

value.rationale: This is an exact structural classification for every cycle size, particle count and positive individual rate profile. A rare-event conditioned process completely forgets rate contrasts except their geometric mean, whereas the survival exponent pays an exact strict AM–GM penalty and the quasi-stationary law records the contrasts. The sharp \(n^{-1}\) weak-disorder window has a nontrivial explicit finite spectral limit. These are natural model observables and constitute more than a routine finite calculation.
